source.title: Variational Learning is Effective for Large Deep Networks
source.authors: Yuesong Shen; Nico Daheim; Bai Cong; Peter Nickl; Gian Maria Marconi; Clement Bazan; Rio Yokota; Iryna Gurevych; D. Cremers; Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan; Thomas Möllenhoff

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out image-classification performance for AdamW and SGD, bearing on whether an adaptive optimizer can perform worse than SGD. The study does not test the claim's other listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on natural-label image classification and GPT-2 validation perplexity. Only the AdamW-versus-SGD image-classification comparisons bear directly on V4. Results about IVON, uncertainty estimation, out-of-distribution performance, model merging, and LOO generalization estimates do not test the listed versions. Cited results from prior work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares AdamW with momentum SGD on held-out image and text classification. Its MC-dropout versus SGD comparison also bears on V6. IVON's performance and generalization estimates do not themselves test the listed claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that IVON makes variational learning effective for large networks, with competitive accuracy, useful uncertainty and downstream applications at costs close to Adam. They attribute AdamW's poor smaller-image-dataset performance to likely overfitting during 200-epoch training; they do not claim a universal adaptive-optimizer disadvantage.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares AdamW and SGD as baselines while evaluating IVON, a variational optimizer; it does not reproduce the original optimizer-comparison studies. Image-classification optimizer hyperparameters were tuned on ResNet-20/CIFAR-10 and then held fixed across other CIFAR and TinyImageNet settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and architecture vary across the reported optimizer comparisons. For CIFAR and TinyImageNet, hyperparameters were tuned on ResNet-20/CIFAR-10 and held fixed across other models and datasets; AdamW required a separate lower learning rate to converge on PreResNet-110/TinyImageNet.

fits_no_version.finding: IVON improves held-out performance and uncertainty relative to several baselines, including AdamW.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Direct variational optimization can train large networks competitively with standard optimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: IVON-based leave-one-out estimates follow test loss more faithfully, and its sensitivity scores identify atypical training images.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Variational covariance estimates can improve generalization prediction and training-data sensitivity estimation.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The paper states that AdamW's smaller-dataset performance is likely due to overfitting when training for 200 epochs. Hyperparameters for CIFAR and TinyImageNet were tuned only on ResNet-20/CIFAR-10; the AdamW result for PreResNet-110 on TinyImageNet converged for only one of five seeds. The study does not measure training-to-test error gaps or random-label memorization.
record.rows_left_out: No additional V4-relevant AdamW-versus-SGD image-classification accuracy pairs were left out from Table 1. Other appendix optimizer comparisons were not extracted because the selected rows already cover the version's tested conditions and the appendix tables add separate architectures and datasets beyond this compact selection.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Controlled widening beyond the width required for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Systematic broader tuning versus limited tuning, switching optimizers, Adam versus AdamW, and word-level language modeling versus SGD. Comparable training performance is not established for the extracted image comparisons.
Batch-size interventions under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout-rate sweeps, very small training sets, excessive-dropout underfitting, and removing dropout together with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance correlated with generalization gaps and ranked against norm or margin measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals.

missing.what: Add MC-dropout versus SGD accuracy rows: 91.85±0.17% versus 91.86±0.14%, state absent for a dropout accuracy benefit. Both use learning rate 0.2; dropout rate is 0.05 and prediction uses 32 samples.

Table 13's omission is broadly declared in rows_left_out, but these text-classification comparisons are needed to represent V4's tested language conditions and their mixed accuracy ordering. Add the CoLA, IMDB and AG News AdamW/SGD pairs used in the text-based verdicts.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. R1/R2 and each subsequent paired row describe the same comparison twice, not independent evidence. Appendix image comparisons and AdaHessian results are declared omissions in rows_left_out. The record incorrectly treats all language comparisons as untested and overlooks the dropout accuracy comparison. Hyperparameter transfer and AdamW convergence failures constrain interpretation; the reported differences do not isolate an intrinsic optimizer effect.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, broader adaptive-optimizer tuning, switching from Adam to SGD, decoupled weight decay, and Adam outperforming on word-level language models.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test-accuracy effects.

source_check.condition: Two-GRU text classifier on AG News, evaluated by accuracy
source_check.reason: Table 13 reports higher accuracy for AdamW, 90.65±0.32% versus 89.57±0.40%, but worse NLL, 0.985±0.046 versus 0.386±0.009. This is a setting and metric exception to V4's qualified claim that adaptive optimizers often perform worse.

relationships.condition: ResNet-20/CIFAR-10, dropout rate 0.05 with MC prediction averaging
relationships.reason: Text-only evidence in Table 2 shows essentially unchanged accuracy: MC dropout 91.85±0.17% versus SGD 91.86±0.14%, despite improved NLL.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy was essentially unchanged while negative log-likelihood improved. This comparison has not been independently checked and combined dropout during training with averaging predictions that vary randomly.
